subject: Model fit signal review and next steps for Novafin
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@novafin.com>, Priya Rao <priya@novafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 17:02:00 -0500
Subject: Model fit signal review and next steps for Novafin

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the eval run: 

Recap from our discovery call
- Primary goal: measure whether open models can hit parity with your current proprietary baseline on customer-facing summarization and entity-extraction tasks.
- Workloads: batch summarization (avg 600 tokens), extraction for billing and contact fragments (~short prompts), and a small control set of few-shot creative completions.
- Success signals discussed: macro accuracy on extraction, human-rated helpfulness (Likert) for summaries, and regression safety checks for hallucinations.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) We’ll deliver a curated prompt set (5k examples subset + 200 human-eval slices) and a runnable eval plan by Monday.
2) Your team to confirm acceptance thresholds (suggested: within 2–3% of baseline on extraction F1; human pass-rate >= 88% on summary helpfulness).
3) Decide host mode for the run (hosted API for speed vs Dedicated for throughput/cost isolation). We can provide estimated spend for both.
4) Schedule a ~90-minute remote run & go/no-go session (we recommend Dec 22–23).

Items I’ll attach / share right after this: prompt-set-novafin-v1.json, a short eval plan, and a link to the benchmark runner.

Open questions for you before we run
- Do you have any specific rubric items we must enforce (safety filters, PII removal rules) beyond the rubric you shared on the call?
- Which Slack channel should we post run updates to (or would you prefer email)?

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation on thresholds and hosting preference and will circulate the prompt set and eval plan shortly.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: prompt-set-novafin-v1.json (prompt set, 5k examples subset)
Attachment: MVP-eval-plan-v1.md (eval plan + run checklist)
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@novafin.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@novafin.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:17:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Model fit signal review and next steps for Novafin

Thanks Dylan — quick responses: 

Appreciate the clear checklist. A few clarifications: 
- Acceptance thresholds: we’re comfortable starting with your suggested band but want to be explicit: parity target = within 2% on extraction F1, and for summaries we want an A/B human eval where open model must be preferred at least 40% of the time vs our baseline (or no worse by >5 points on the Likert).
- Rubric: I’m attaching the product rubric we use for customer-facing summaries. Please ensure the eval enforces the “no financial hallucination” check.
- Hosting: prefer hosted for the initial pass (faster setup), but include a Dedicated cost estimate in the run doc so procurement can evaluate.

One ask: can you include a small, red-team prompt subset for hallucination testing? We care a lot about regressions there.

If you can share the cost delta and a planned run calendar by EOD Monday, we’ll confirm the Dec 22 slot.

Thanks —
Oliver
Director of Product | Novafin

Attachment: Novafin-rubric.pdf (product rubric, highlights no-financial-hallucination rule)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: internal — model candidates & quick benchmark notes for Novafin

Dylan / Tessa — internal notes and recommended config for the Novafin run (do not forward; this is internal ops):

Model candidates (shortlist)
- open: Mistral-7B-Std (v0.2) — strong for extraction, low latency.
- open: Llama-2-70B-QLoRA (quantized) — better on abstractive summarization but higher cost.
- redwood baseline: redwood-std-3b (our in-house tuned baseline) — consistent on safety and hallucination filters.

Evaluation plan highlights
- Batch size: 8 for hosted, 32 for Dedicated cold-run (to estimate throughput).
- Metrics: Extraction F1, Summary Likert preference (A/B), hallucination rate (percentage of outputs with fabricated numeric facts), token cost estimate per 1k requests.
- Red-team subset: 250 prompts (hard prompts that trigger hallucinations) included in prompt-set-novafin-v1.json.

Benchmarks (internal links)
- Raw run: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/novafin/2026-12-run (contains CSV with per-prompt metrics)
- Quick CSV: novafin-benchmarks-20261219.csv (attached)

Notes on parity handling
- If open model extraction F1 is within 2% of baseline but summary preference lags by >5 points, recommend a paired evaluation with lightweight prompt-engineering first (no immediate quantization or ensembling).
- Any hallucination regression >1% absolute on the red-team subset should block rollout. We should include an automated fail flag in the runner for that case.

Attachments: prompt-set-novafin-v1.json, novafin-benchmarks-20261219.csv

Marissa Cole
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@novafin.com>, Priya Rao <priya@novafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Model fit signal review and next steps for Novafin

Oliver / Priya — thanks for the rubric and the quick turn. Short answers and final plan: 

- Acceptance thresholds: we’ll use the working thresholds you confirmed (extraction F1 within 2%; summary A/B must not be worse by >5 points; red-team hallucination <=1% absolute). We’ll include the exact checks in the MVP-eval-plan-v1.md.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: we’ll run the initial pass on Hosted for speed and attach a Dedicated cost appendix. Expect ~18% higher cost but lower median latency on Dedicated for the large Llama-2 run. Cost appendix will be in the shared Drive link.
- Red-team prompts: included (250 prompts).
- Calendar: proposed run window Dec 22 14:00–16:00 ET. Please confirm and we’ll reserve infra.

Next visible deliverables (we’ll share links/copies in HubSpot and Drive):
- prompt-set-novafin-v1.json (you already have)
- MVP-eval-plan-v1.md (attached)
- Quick benchmark runner results link: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/novafin/2026-12-run
- Cost appendix: will be posted to Drive by EOD Monday

Owner map
- Run owner / day-of contact: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.ai)
- Technical contact for integration/questions: Tessa Morgan (tessa@redwood.ai)
- Commercial / procurement: Dylan Brooks (me) — will send Dedicated pricing appendix to Priya.

If that sounds good, confirm the Dec 22 slot and I’ll send calendar invites.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: MVP-eval-plan-v1.md (eval checklist and automated fail criteria)
